done_when: When core.hooksPath is husky's folder, forge sync puts one line that runs Forge's pre-commit and pre-push checks (through .forge/hooks.sh) into the repo's committed .husky/pre-commit and .husky/pre-push, keeping their existing lines, and writes no shims into the folder husky rebuilds; the checks still run after npm install rebuilds that folder, in every worktree and a fresh clone; doctor reports the hooks installed in that setup; repos without husky keep today's shims; command tests cover a new husky repo and a husky repo adopted on an earlier release (including its earlier .pre-forge shims cleaned up)

findings.body: Both committed hooks source the launcher before running the user script. The launcher at src/forge/sync.py:78–81 prepends global executable folders, overriding Husky's deliberate `node_modules/.bin` priority (tests/fixtures/husky-v9.1.7/husky:16). This child shell inherits that modified PATH. Consequently, an existing `eslint .` hook runs a globally installed ESLint instead of the repository's pinned executable when both exist; similarly, global Node can override the version selected by Husky's initialization. Preserve the incoming PATH for user commands and apply Forge's launcher PATH only to Forge.
findings.title: Preserve Husky's PATH when running existing user hooks

findings.body: An absolute core.hooksPath pointing to the original checkout's `.husky/_` passes this check there, but Git shares that configuration with linked worktrees. Upgrade creates another checkout at src/forge/upgrade.py:99 and runs sync there at line 146, where this guard now refuses the same configuration because its folder lies outside the new checkout. Close's verification checkout (src/forge/close.py:362–364) and oversized-fix inventory (src/forge/sync.py:369) encounter the same problem. This is new operational evidence beyond the ruling about detecting absolute paths inside the checkout: those accepted configurations cannot complete routine worktree-based workflows. Handle that configuration explicitly while retaining protection against outside links.
findings.title: Handle absolute Husky paths during worktree-based upgrade and close

why: In client repos that use husky, every npm install rebuilds husky's hooks folder (core.hooksPath .husky/_) and wipes Forge's pre-commit and pre-push shims, so doctor reports the git hooks missing in every worktree after install (reported by a client session on v1.2.7). Owner decision 2026-10-08: add Forge to husky's own committed hooks
